display: Annie Oakley was born Phoebe Ann Moses (also spelled Mosey) on August 13, 1860, in Darke County, Ohio, to Jacob Moses and Susan Wise Moses.
Her father died when she was six; two sources give pneumonia as the cause, and the Garst Museum says he died from exposure to winter weather. Her mother was left to support a large family.
She became a celebrated exhibition sharpshooter who toured with a Wild West show in the United States and Europe, and in later years she gave exhibitions and taught women to shoot.
On October 29, 1901, the show's train collided head-on with another train in North Carolina; Oakley's back was injured, and the accident ended her touring with the show.

Late in 1922 she was severely injured in an automobile accident in Florida, reported as fractures of the hip and ankle, after which she had to wear a brace on her leg; her recovery took more than a year.
Her health declined in the years after the accident, and in 1925 she moved back to Darke County, Ohio.
Oakley died on November 3, 1926, in Greenville, Ohio, aged 66; the Garst Museum and HistoryNet give pernicious anemia as the cause of death.
